messages.subject: binary variables and fiml
parts:
Hello,
I am trying to use lavaan's CFA function for a model with a number of binary indicators. I first ran the code below so that the indicators of the DVs would be recognized as ordered.

data[,c("T2Q2","T2Q11", "T2Q50","T2Q56","T2Q57", "T2Q1")] <-lapply(data[,c("T2Q2","T2Q11", "T2Q50","T2Q56","T2Q57", "T2Q1")], ordered)

Next, I tried to run my model. I'm attempting to use FIML. 

#############################
# Configural invariance model 
############################

config<- '
grade1 =~ NA*T1Q1
gender1=~ NA*T1Q2
cellphone1=~NA*T1Q11
timecell1=~NA*T1Q19
fb1_1=~ NA*T1Q319 
fb2_1=~NA*T1Q50 
fb3_1=~ NA*T1Q52
passfriend1=~NA*T1Q191
gotube1=~NA*T1Q56
posttube1=~NA*T1Q57
parpass1=~NA*T1Q65
grade2 =~ NA*T2Q1
gender2=~ NA*T2Q2
cellphone2=~NA*T2Q11
timecell2=~NA*T2Q19
fb2_2=~NA*T2Q50 
fb3_2=~ NA*T2Q52
passfriend2=~NA*T2Q191
gotube2=~NA*T2Q56
posttube2=~NA*T2Q57
moraldis1 =~ t1md1parc + t1md2parc + t1md3parc 
moraldis2 =~ t2md1parc + t2md2parc + t2md3parc
timeint1 =~ v1*T1Q9 + v1*T1Q10
timeint2 =~ v2*T2Q9 + v2*T2Q10
cmonitor1=~ T1Q155 + T1Q156 + T1Q157 + T1Q158
cmonitor2=~ T2Q155 + T2Q156 + T2Q157 + T2Q158
pmonitor1 =~ T1P156 + T1P157 + T1P158
pmonitor2 =~ T2P156 + T2P157 + T2P158
cvict1 =~ T1Q201 + T1Q202 + T1Q204 
cvict2 =~ T2Q201 + T2Q202 + T2Q204
tvic1 =~ T1Q72 + T1Q73 + T1Q74 
tvic2 =~ T2Q72 + T2Q73 + T2Q74 
tbul1=~ T1Q80 + T1Q82 + T1Q83
tbul2=~ T2Q80 + T2Q82 + T2Q83 
cbul1 =~ T1Q197 + T1Q198 + T1Q199 
cbul2 =~ T2Q197 + T2Q198 + T2Q199 

moraldis1 ~~ moraldis2
timeint1 ~~ timeint2
cmonitor1 ~~ cmonitor2
pmonitor1 ~~pmonitor2
cvict1~~cvict2
tvic1~~tvic2
tbul1~~tbul2
cbul1~~cbul2'

fitconfig<- cfa(config, data=data, missing='fiml', meanstructure=T, std.lv=TRUE)
summary(fitconfig, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

I got this error:

Error in muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  : 
  unknown ov.types:character


I tried switching the estimator. I thought that since lavaan automatically switches the estimator, maybe it would help to try it manually since I have also asked for FIML.

fitconfig<- cfa(config, data=data, missing='fiml', meanstructure=T, std.lv=TRUE, estimator="WLSMV")

Then I got this error:

Error in lav_options_set(opt) : 
  lavaan ERROR: missing="ml" is not allowed for estimator MLM, MLMV, GLS, ULS, ULSM, ULSMV, DWLS, WLS, WLSM, WLSMV, PML

Is there a way to use the cfa function with FIML and binary variables at the same time? Did I actually make a mistake earlier that is causing the errors?

Thank you very much in advance for any help you can provide.

Diana

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: binary variables and fiml
parts: Is there a way to use the cfa function with FIML and binary variables at the same time?

Specifying missing = "fiml" (FIML stands for "full-information maximum likelihood") is implying that you want to use maximum likelihood estimation, not WLSMV.  There is no analog for FIML when using weighted least squares.  If your data had several ordered categories (at least 5), it might be feasible to simply treat them as continuous and adjust for non-normality using the MLR estimator, but I do not think it would appropriate to do so for binary data.  Your best option would be to use multiple imputation instead.  There is a function in the semTools package that automates the imputation, analysis, and combination of parameters and SEs. 

install.packages("semTools")
library(semTools)
?cfa.mi

Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: binary variables and fiml
parts:
> I got this error:
>
> Error in muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types =
> ov.types, :
> unknown ov.types:character

No this worries me: do you have a variable that contains 'characters'
(instead of numbers)? You can use the varTable() function on your
data.frame to see which variable is of type 'character'.

> Is there a way to use the cfa function with FIML and binary variables at
> the same time?

Not yet. Once estimator = "MML" (marginal ML) is ready for prime time,
it should be able to use fiml.

Yves.
